title: Machine Learning Applications for Data Center Optimization
notes: Neural-network model of PUE from plant telemetry (about 19 inputs) used to simulate what-if setpoint changes; the origin story of ML for DC cooling. URL and bibliographic details are from memory and not page-verified.

title: DeepMind AI Reduces Google Data Centre Cooling Bill by 40%
notes: Announces a recommendation system (humans apply the suggested setpoints) that cut cooling energy by up to 40 percent; vendor blog, so treat the headline as a best-case figure from one facility.

title: Safety-first AI for autonomous data centre cooling and industrial control
notes: Moves from recommendations to direct autonomous control with layered safety (uncertainty estimates, hard operating constraints, operator override); good template for the safety section of the cooling capstone.

title: Data center cooling using model-predictive control
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31 (NeurIPS 2018)
notes: Learns a linear time-varying dynamics model from about two years of sensor data and runs MPC with safety constraints, comparing favourably with a deep-RL baseline for data efficiency. Exact paper URL still to be pinned; the proceedings are open.

title: Controlling Commercial Cooling Systems Using Reinforcement Learning
notes: Live RL control of two real commercial chiller plants with roughly 9 and 13 percent energy savings; the most useful part for the course is the discussion of evaluation, offline learning and constraint handling in real deployments.

title: Simulator-based reinforcement learning for data center cooling optimization
notes: Describes training RL on a physics simulator of Meta's outside-air/evaporative penthouse cooling and reporting about 20 percent lower supply-fan energy and 4 percent less water in a pilot region; direct precedent for capstone 1's simulate-then-deploy design.

title: Carbon-Aware Computing for Datacenters
notes: Google's carbon-intelligent compute management: day-ahead load and carbon-intensity forecasts feed a risk-aware optimizer producing hourly Virtual Capacity Curves that defer flexible jobs. Good example of forecast-then-optimize.

title: Dynamo: Facebook's Data Center-Wide Power Management System
notes: Hierarchical power-capping and oversubscription at Facebook; non-ML but defines the control problem (priority-aware capping against breaker limits). Crossref confirmed; I did not locate a verified open PDF.

title: Data Center Power Oversubscription with a Medium Voltage Power Plane and Priority-Aware Capping
venue: Proceedings of the 25th International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS 2020)
notes: Companion paper to Google's public 2019 power-trace dataset (57 power domains). Author list and DOI are from memory; the URL is the one cited by the dataset's own README (page-verified via that README).

title: Resource Central: Understanding and Predicting Workloads for Improved Resource Management in Large Cloud Platforms
notes: Azure's ML service predicting VM lifetime, size and utilization with gradient-boosted trees to drive placement and oversubscription; companion to the Azure public traces. Open copy (Microsoft Research) likely exists; confirm via library.

title: Predicting Disk Replacement towards Reliable Data Centers
notes: Disk replacement prediction with class imbalance and time-aware evaluation; use with the Backblaze data to teach leakage-safe survival-style splits.

title: Backblaze Drive Stats
license: Backblaze terms: cite Backblaze; user responsible for use; derivative works may be sold but the data itself may not be resold
notes: Daily SMART snapshots for every drive since 2013, updated quarterly (Q2 2026 snapshot lists 354,415 drives). Best public hardware-failure dataset.

title: The ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III competition: Overview and results
venue: Science and Technology for the Built Environment
notes: Overview of the Kaggle competition on predicting meter readings for 2,380 meters; winners relied on gradient boosting ensembles and heavy handling of data quality and leakage. The arXiv id is from memory (the BDG2 README says a preprint is on arXiv).

title: The Building Data Genome Project 2, energy meter data from the ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III competition
notes: Data descriptor for BDG2: 3,053 meters in 1,636 non-residential buildings, hourly, 2016 to 2017. Primary dataset for the building-load forecasting modules.

title: Building Data Genome Project 2 v1.0 (Zenodo)
notes: 595 MB zip; Zenodo API record confirms CC BY 4.0 licence.

title: Probabilistic energy forecasting: Global Energy Forecasting Competition 2014 and beyond
notes: Competition report for quantile forecasting of load, price, wind and solar using pinball loss; the reference for probabilistic energy forecast evaluation.

title: The M4 Competition: 100,000 time series and 61 forecasting methods
notes: Key finding for the course: statistical/ML hybrids and ensembles beat pure ML, and simple combinations are strong baselines.

title: M5 accuracy competition: Results, findings, and conclusions
notes: Retail demand competition won by LightGBM-style gradient boosting with strong feature engineering; supports teaching GBMs for tabular forecasting.

title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
notes: Tokenizes scaled values and trains T5 models; reports zero-shot accuracy comparable to, and sometimes better than, models trained per dataset across 42 datasets. Code is Apache-2.0.

title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
notes: TimesFM: patched decoder pretrained on a large corpus with zero-shot accuracy near supervised models on public benchmarks.

title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers
notes: Moirai plus the LOTSA pretraining archive (27B observations); any-variate attention.

title: TimeGPT-1
notes: Commercial API foundation forecaster; closed weights so results cannot be independently reproduced offline. Use as a cautionary example.

title: GIFT-Eval: A Benchmark For General Time Series Forecasting Model Evaluation
notes: 23 datasets, 144k series, with a non-leaking pretraining set; compares 17 baselines and discusses where foundation models do and do not win. Use for the leakage lesson (train/test overlap in foundation-model evals).

title: Are Language Models Actually Useful for Time Series Forecasting?
notes: Ablations show that removing the pretrained LLM from LLM-adapted forecasters does not hurt and often helps; strong evidence for keeping tuned baselines in every comparison.

title: Anomaly detection: A survey
notes: Canonical taxonomy (point, contextual, collective anomalies; supervised, semi-supervised, unsupervised); use as the vocabulary for module 22.

title: Isolation Forest
notes: Random-partition isolation as an anomaly score; fast, no distance computation. Baseline detector for sensor data.

title: Methods for Fault Detection, Diagnostics, and Prognostics for Building Systems: A Review, Part I
notes: Standard HVAC FDD taxonomy (model-based, rule-based, data-driven). Part II is DOI 10.1080/10789669.2005.10391134 (not independently verified). A PNNL/OSTI copy probably exists; the open_url is a placeholder to resolve.

title: Building fault detection data to aid diagnostic algorithm creation and performance testing
notes: Data descriptor for the labeled LBNL/PNNL/NREL/ORNL HVAC FDD datasets. Author list is partly from memory; title, first author, year confirmed via Crossref.

title: LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets
license: Publicly accessible via OEDI; check the page's license field before redistribution
notes: Time-series data with faults at several severities plus fault-free cases for seven equipment types (RTU, single- and dual-duct AHU, VAV, FCU, chiller plant, boiler plant), with PDFs and Brick TTL files.

title: An Expert Rule Set for Fault Detection in Air-Handling Units
notes: AHU rule set (APAR) from IEA Annex 25; a template for hand-written physics rules that an LLM agent can call as tools. Title and venue from memory; verify via the library. Citation record verified on the NIST publications page; full text is in ASHRAE Transactions (library access).

title: Evaluating Real-time Anomaly Detection Algorithms - the Numenta Anomaly Benchmark
notes: Streaming benchmark with a scoring function that rewards early detection and penalizes false alarms; data and code are MIT on GitHub.

title: Current Time Series Anomaly Detection Benchmarks are Flawed and are Creating the Illusion of Progress
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
notes: Argues that Yahoo, Numenta, NASA and similar benchmarks have triviality, unrealistic anomaly density, mislabeling and run-to-failure bias; introduces the UCR Anomaly Archive.

title: Anomaly detection in time series: a comprehensive evaluation
notes: Compares 71 detectors on many datasets; shows no method dominates, simple methods are often competitive, and metric choice changes rankings. Use to justify a multi-metric harness.

title: Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations
notes: Original PINN paper: embed PDE residuals in the loss. Good for heat-transfer examples; course should also teach its known training pathologies.

title: Physics-informed machine learning
notes: Review organizing physics-informed ML into observational, inductive and learning biases; use as the map for module 24's physics-informed section.

title: Discovering governing equations from data by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems
notes: SINDy: sparse regression on a library of candidate terms to recover ODEs; arXiv id from memory. Useful for identifying simple thermal dynamics from data.

title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
notes: Parameterizes the derivative of a hidden state with a network and integrates with an ODE solver; the basis for continuous-time learned plant models.

title: Identifying suitable models for the heat dynamics of buildings
notes: Forward model selection among lumped RC (grey-box) stochastic models using likelihood tests; the practical recipe for RC thermal models. DOI confirmed through a Crossref search result, not a direct lookup.

title: Physics-constrained deep learning of multi-zone building thermal dynamics
notes: Structured neural state-space model with physics-inspired constraints for building thermal dynamics (a PNNL work, so an OSTI copy is likely). Author list from memory.

title: Foundational Research Gaps and Future Directions for Digital Twins
authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
notes: Consensus report defining a digital twin as a bidirectional coupling of virtual and physical systems and emphasizing verification, validation and uncertainty quantification; use to scope the capstone's 'digital twin' claim honestly.

title: All you need to know about model predictive control for buildings
notes: The standard review of MPC for buildings: modelling, estimation, formulation, deployment cost and open problems. Author list partly from memory.

title: Theory and applications of HVAC control systems - A review of model predictive control (MPC)
notes: Earlier review of MPC for HVAC, including simulated versus real savings; useful for the comparison with newer RL reviews.

title: Reinforcement learning for building controls: The opportunities and challenges
notes: LBNL review covering how RL was applied to buildings and the practical barriers (sample efficiency, safety, simulators); a LBNL/eScholarship open copy is likely.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Building HVAC Control
notes: Early deep Q-learning for HVAC in EnergyPlus; useful as a historical example whose evaluation conditions are easy to critique.

title: Gnu-RL: A Precocial Reinforcement Learning Solution for Building HVAC Control Using a Differentiable MPC Policy
notes: Policy is a differentiable MPC initialized by imitation of an existing controller, bridging MPC and RL. Title from memory; Crossref confirmed first author, year and short title.

title: Building optimization testing framework (BOPTEST) for simulation-based benchmarking of control strategies in buildings
notes: Containerized Modelica emulators with standard KPIs for comparing controllers; the most credible benchmark for MPC versus RL on buildings. Author list partly from memory.

title: Sinergym: A Building Simulation and Control Framework for Training Reinforcement Learning Agents
notes: Gymnasium wrapper around EnergyPlus (code MIT per GitHub API). Includes data-center-like environments in later versions (not verified).

title: CityLearn v1.0: An OpenAI Gym Environment for Demand Response with Deep Reinforcement Learning
notes: Multi-building demand-response RL environment (MIT licence per GitHub API).

title: CityLearn v2: Energy-flexible, resilient, occupant-centric, and carbon-aware management of grid-interactive communities
notes: CityLearn built on the NREL End-Use Load Profiles dataset, with RL, MPC and rule-based baselines for batteries, V2G and heat pumps.

title: Safe Learning in Robotics: From Learning-Based Control to Safe Reinforcement Learning
venue: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems 5
notes: Survey of safe learning for physical systems (constraint satisfaction, safety filters, certification); transferable to HVAC and cooling control. arXiv id from memory.

title: AssetOpsBench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Task Automation in Industrial Asset Operations and Maintenance
notes: IBM benchmark: four domain agents, 140+ human-written queries and a simulated CouchDB IoT environment, scored with an automated evaluation of Tool-As-Agent versus Plan-Executor designs. Closest public template for capstone 2's harness; vendor-authored, so check for overfitting to its own tools.

title: Automated Root Causing of Cloud Incidents using In-Context Learning with GPT-4
notes: Microsoft study of retrieval of similar historical incidents plus in-context learning for root-causing cloud incidents; closest analogue to retrieval-based fault diagnosis. Only the first author was recorded from the arXiv feed.

title: LogEval: A Comprehensive Benchmark Suite for Large Language Models In Log Analysis
notes: Benchmark of LLMs on log parsing, anomaly detection and fault diagnosis for IT logs; pattern for building an eval set from logs. Only the first author was recorded.

title: Consultation on Industrial Machine Faults with Large language Models
notes: Small preprint on using LLMs to advise on machine faults; low-credibility, include only as a weak data point. Title and first author verified via the arXiv feed; I did not read the paper.

title: Google cluster-data (ClusterData2011, ClusterData2019, PowerData2019)
license: CC-BY 4.0 (stated in the 2019 cluster and power trace docs)
notes: Borg traces for 8 cells in May 2019 plus 2019 power traces for 57 power domains in Google data centers, with a Colab to reproduce the paper's figures.

title: Azure Public Dataset (VM, LLM inference, Copilot agent traces)
notes: Includes VM traces plus LLM inference traces (Nov 2023, May 2024), multimodal inference traces (Oct 2024) and a GitHub Copilot coding-agent trace, per its README.

title: Alibaba cluster-trace (v2017, v2018 and later)
license: No licence file in repository; read each trace's terms
notes: v2017 covers about 1,300 machines over 12 hours with co-located online and batch work; later versions add GPU and other traces.

title: Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (NAB)
notes: 58 labeled streaming series; use as a demonstration of why the Wu and Keogh critique matters.

title: SKAB: Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark
notes: Water-circulation testbed with labeled anomalies; GPL-3.0 licence means check compatibility before bundling. Author names from memory.

title: EIA Open Data API (including Hourly Electric Grid Monitor, EIA-930)
license: Free; API key registration and Terms of Service; follow EIA Copyrights and Reuse Policy
notes: Page confirms free access via a registered API key; hourly balancing-authority demand, generation by fuel and interchange (EIA-930) are inside the electricity section.

title: WattTime Data Signals overview
license: API terms; registration required; free access scope not verified
notes: Marginal operating emissions rate (co2_moer) signal in lbs/MWh with forecasts for load shifting; check free-tier coverage and terms before relying on it.
